MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Fleetwood Mac and Neil Diamond feel like natural next choices because I am looking for familiar, melodic older songs collected in one place.",
    "The Lovin' Spoonful and 5th Dimension fit the tuneful pop and vocal harmonies I enjoy in my mid-'60s collections and Simon & Garfunkel listening.",
    "The Christmas collection fits my recent interest in A Very Special Christmas and feels relevant to what I want to hear now."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "A Decade of Hits 1969-1979, Greatest Hits, and The United Artists Collection leave me unsure whose music I would be choosing; an appealing era or collection title alone is not enough.",
    "Songs Of Cindy Walker does not connect as closely to the older pop and classic rock collections I want right now.",
    "Graceland appeals to me through my Simon & Garfunkel listening, but that connection is weaker than my current desire for a collection of familiar hits."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "The recommendations seem to assume that any greatest-hits collection will appeal to me, when the performer and recognizable music matter more than the label.",
    "Older music is treated as broadly interchangeable, even though I am drawn to particular melodies, harmonies, and familiar performers."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My repeated interest in best-of collections reflects a desire for familiar songs, so a related artist's individual album is appealing without necessarily being my next choice.",
    "Knowing the performer or songs matters to my decision; vague collection titles do not give me enough reason to choose them.",
    "My recent Christmas listening matters alongside my longstanding interest in older pop and classic rock."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations understood my interest in familiar older pop and classic rock, but sometimes treated an era or compilation title as enough evidence that I would want the music."
}
